title: Moana and the ocean.
lines: On a beautiful island in the big ocean lives a girl.
Her name is Moana.
The island is called Motunui.
There are palm trees with coconuts, there are white beaches and the water is clear and blue.
Moana's daddy is the chief of the island.
And one day Moana will be the chief.
Moana loves the ocean.
She has since she was very little.
Every day she stands on the beach and watches the waves.
She really wants to go out to sea.
But her daddy always says: No, Moana.
Nobody goes past the reef.
The sea is dangerous.
Moana has a grandma.
Grandma Tala.
Grandma Tala loves to dance with the waves, and she tells the most beautiful stories.
Grandma is the only one who understands how much Moana loves the sea.
One day something strange happens on the island.
The coconuts are brown and soft inside.
The fishermen don't catch any more fish.
The island is getting sick.
Grandma Tala takes Moana to a secret cave.
Inside there are big, old boats.
Look, says Grandma.
Long ago our ancestors were voyagers.
They sailed across the whole ocean.
They found their way with the stars.
Grandma gives Moana a small, green stone.
It glows a little.
This is the heart of Te Fiti, says Grandma.
Te Fiti is the island that gives life to everything.
But long ago the heart was stolen by the demigod Maui.
That's why our island is getting sick.
You must find Maui, and together you must bring the heart back.
Moana is scared.
But she is also brave.
One night, when everyone is asleep, she gets into a small boat.
She takes her rooster with her, Heihei.
Heihei is a bit silly.
He eats pebbles and always bumps into things.
Moana sails out to sea, past the reef.
The waves are big.
The wind blows hard.
But Moana keeps going.
And the ocean helps her.
The water is a little bit magical.
It pushes her boat in the right direction.
After a long journey Moana finds a small island.
Maui lives there.
Maui is big and strong, with long curls and drawings on his skin.
He has a big hook.
With it he can turn into animals.
Into a hawk, a shark, or even a lizard.
Maui is a bit of a show-off.
I am Maui!
he says.
I caught the sun and pulled islands out of the sea!
Moana says: And you stole the heart of Te Fiti.
Bring it back!
At first Maui doesn't want to.
But Moana keeps asking.
And she is so brave that in the end Maui helps her.
Together they sail on.
Maui teaches Moana how to find the way with the stars.
And how to turn the sail in the wind.
Moana learns quickly.
Then they come to Te Fiti.
But there stands a big fire mountain.
It is angry and hot.
It throws fire and ash.
Maui wants to fight.
But Moana sees something.
On the fire monster's chest there is a hole, exactly in the shape of a spiral.
The heart fits in it!
Moana walks very calmly towards the monster.
She isn't afraid.
She sings softly.
The monster goes quiet.
I know who you are, says Moana.
You are Te Fiti.
You're only angry because you lost your heart.
She puts the green stone in the hole.
And then something wonderful happens.
The fire goes out.
The monster turns into a green woman, full of flowers and plants.
It's Te Fiti!
Flowers and trees grow everywhere.
Maui says sorry.
Te Fiti forgives him.
Moana sails back home.
On Motunui the coconuts are white and fresh again.
There are fish again.
Her daddy hugs her.
You are a real voyager, he says proudly.
And from that day on the people of Motunui sail across the ocean again.
With Moana in front.
The end.
